frequency_question: How often do major energy/infrastructure bills enacted by Congress successfully include specific, enforceable language streamlining interstate project approvals without getting stripped or overly generalized?
membership_rule: Members are major federal energy or infrastructure packages signed into law between 1995 and 2024. Excluded are minor standalone non-substantive resolutions and bills that failed to pass.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major legislative vehicles examined; all successfully preserved text meeting the criteria when substantive consensus was reached.
known_gaps: Excludes minor committee-level riders that failed to reach the floor.
skeleton: Enacted major energy/infrastructure packages containing permitting language divided by total major enacted energy/infrastructure packages in modern congressional history.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 major enacted omnibus packages containing targeted permitting provisions over the target window.
validity_reason: Legislative drafting standards and statutory inclusion norms for omnibus packages remain consistent across recent congressional sessions.
